hints: Focus on the carbon on the right side of the ring (carbon 1, the anomeric carbon) and notice whether its OH points down below the ring or up above the ring.
Check the CH2OH group is up on the top left, and the OH on the left side carbon is down, this confirms it is glucose and not galactose, then down on carbon 1 means alpha.
walkthrough:
**Spot the glucose skeleton**

Look for a six-membered pyranose ring with CH2OH on the top left pointing up. All four diagrams have this, so all are hexoses.

Now look at the left side carbon (carbon 4). In glucose this OH points down.

**Rule out galactose**

In diagrams A, B and C the left side shows HO pointing down and out, so carbon 4 OH is down. That is glucose.

In diagram D the HO is drawn up on the top left, so carbon 4 OH is up. That is galactose, not glucose.

**Use carbon 1 to tell alpha from beta**

The carbon on the far right is carbon 1. The rule is simple:
$$ \text{alpha-glucose: C1-OH down (below ring)} $$
$$ \text{beta-glucose: C1-OH up (above ring)} $$
Only diagram A has the C1 OH pointing down below the ring while keeping the glucose pattern at carbons 2, 3 and 4. That is alpha-glucose.

options.A: Correct. CH2OH is up, carbon 4 OH is down for glucose, and carbon 1 OH is down for alpha. This is alpha-glucose.
options.B: False. The OH on carbon 1 is positioned above the ring, giving the beta arrangement, not alpha.
options.C: False. The OH on carbon 1 is clearly drawn up above the ring on the right, which is beta-glucose.
options.D: False. The OH on the left side carbon 4 points up, which is the pattern for galactose, not glucose.
